headline: Serbia's students won. The strongman conceded.
summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded on Sunday night, about 90 minutes after the polls closed. His party projects the Students' List at 135 to 140 of the 250 seats, his own at around 105. The movement grew out of a train station canopy that fell in Novi Sad in 2024 and killed 16. Belgrade filled with car horns and fireworks.
cover_answer: Not kids. University students, and grown-ups they picked.
table_question: If you lost a vote fair and square, would you say so out loud?

5-7.script: In a country called Serbia, far across the ocean, university students spent two years asking the government to fix things. Today the whole country voted, and the students' side won. The man who had been in charge for 14 years said out loud that he lost. People danced in the streets and set off fireworks, like the Fourth of July.
5-7.why: A vote, a loss said out loud, a party in the street. The fireworks are the picture they keep.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the fireworks and the man saying out loud that he lost. The canopy and the 16 dead stay in the Try answer; Cantor found this age fears what it can picture. Expect "can that happen here?" Yes. We vote too, and the loser says so.

8-12.script: In 2024 a concrete canopy fell at a train station in Novi Sad and killed 16 people. Students blamed corruption in the repairs, marched for two years, then put up their own list for Sunday's vote. Vucic's party projects them at 135 to 140 of 250 seats. Like a class vote: pass half and you set the rules.
8-12.why: Canopy, blame, march, ballot, seats: a chain with a number at the end.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script hands them the chain: a canopy falls, students blame the repairs, two years of marches, then a ballot and 135 seats. Half of 250 is arithmetic they can do. Expect "did the students get in trouble?" Vucic called them foreign-led. They won anyway.

13-17.script: Would you trust a strongman who concedes 90 minutes after the polls close? Vucic did, then blamed independent media, European countries and an "American deep state." The Students' List put no student on its ballot and campaigned with no leader. Can a movement with no leader govern?
13-17.why: Two things to argue: a quick loser who blames everyone, a winner with no leader.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Vucic conceded within two hours and blamed an "American deep state" for it. The script hands them that pair, then a harder one, whether a list with no leader can run a country, which nobody knows yet. Expect "so who's in charge now?" Nobody yet. The seats are projections.

5-7.a: Not kids. University students built the group and picked farmers, athletes and artists to run. Grown-ups voted for them.

8-12.q: Why did a train station make people so angry?
8-12.a: Just renovated, it fell and killed 16. Protesters blamed corruption in the work.

8-12.q: How many seats do you need to win?
8-12.a: More than half of 250, so 126. The students' side is projected at 135 to 140.

13-17.q: Why did he concede so fast?
13-17.a: The AP doesn't say. His own count: 2.2 million votes to 1.7 million.
Not settled. The list's lead candidate is a cardiologist, Ilija Srdanovic.
